subject: Mythology
title: The Chocolate Myth: Gift of the Gods
description: A 60-second lesson on The Chocolate Myth: Gift of the Gods.

hook.text: Chocolate was considered so sacred in Mesoamerica that only gods, kings, and warriors were allowed to drink it.

buildup.text: Quetzalcoatl stole cacao from the gods and gave it to humans. It was consumed as a bitter, spicy ceremonial drink.

discovery.text: Cacao beans were used as currency. You could buy a rabbit for ten beans or a slave for a hundred.

twist.text: The word 'chocolate' comes from the Nahuatl word 'xocolatl.' Every chocolate bar traces back to Mesoamerican gods.

climax.text: The Spanish added sugar and took it to Europe, launching a global obsession worth over $130 billion today.

punchline.text: A god stole a bean, and now the whole world is addicted to it.

quiz.question: How was chocolate originally consumed in Mesoamerica?
options: As a sweet candy given to children
As a bitter, spicy ceremonial drink for elites
As a powder mixed into bread and pastries
